dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi there, are you here for The Crux Clash too?

dialogues.speaker: Chai Yi
dialogues.text: That's right. Nothing beats real-life combat for honing your skills. That's what our master taught us.

dialogues.speaker: Chai Yi
dialogues.text: But this tournament is more than just a chance to put training into practice — it's also a chance for us to obtain the Masterless Vision.

dialogues.speaker: Liang
dialogues.text: Exactly! With a Vision, we'd quickly become our master's top students.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This master of yours must be pretty incredible, huh... Are they someone famous?

dialogues.speaker: Chai Yi
dialogues.text: Famous? He's the founder of the Lingshan Clan, and his skills are unparalleled! Liang and I are both proud disciples of his.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: You probably wouldn't have heard of it, it was founded quite recently. The clan is nowhere near as famous as the master himself, anyway.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: He's got to be a grandmaster or something. He's created many different styles of kung fu, and countless other clans have borrowed extensively from him.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: To the Lingshan Clan, he teaches a special technique known as "force dispersal."

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: It's a type of breathing exercise where you can train yourself to harness the energy around you and neutralize attacks without moving an inch.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: For example, our master can use it to alter the path of an attacking fist, or change the direction of an incoming stone, all without breaking a sweat!

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: One time, he sent a challenger flying into the air without lifting a finger!

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: It sure is! But it's extremely difficult to cultivate this ability. We've been training for ages, and we're still getting to grips with the very basics. There's no way we could use it proficiently yet.

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: *sigh* We're clearly not that naturally gifted, or we would have at least gotten the gist by now... If we don't start making progress soon, we'll probably run out of money to pay the tuition fees and still have nothing to show for all our training...

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: Of course! This is a grandmaster we're talking about here. He doesn't have time to waste. If you want face-to-face training, you've gotta show you're sincere about it.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: *sigh* But here we are, having trained under him directly all this time without even a hint of improvement. Master is getting increasingly impatient with us.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: Recently, though, we heard that a Vision bearer joined the Guhua Clan and made pretty much instant progress in their training.

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: So, if we can get our hands on a Vision, too, maybe we can finally make our master proud!

choices.text: A Vision won't make you better at martial arts.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: Well, we have to try something new, otherwise, we're stuck in the same situation.

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: Exactly, it can't hurt to try. And if it turns out it does work, the Lingshan Clan will go down in history!

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: Folks will come from far and wide. Heck, we could even become the dominant martial arts clan in all of Liyue!

choices.text: There may be other reasons why you can't seem to master this technique...

dialogues.speaker: Chai Yi
dialogues.text: If we win... we could even start our own clan and take disciples of our own!

dialogues.speaker: Liang
dialogues.text: Keep your voice down! What if the master heard you'd been saying something like that, huh?
